You are on the support-desk Genkit app in this directory. Bug report: On the refund desk a customer wrote "I want a refund for order A-1001, it arrived broken." The desk asked for approval as usual, and the supervisor declined it as a duplicate claim. After that the desk never gives the customer a final answer: it fails, asks for approval again, or keeps working on the order. A declined refund should end with a short reply to the customer.
Find the root cause and fix it in the app's source. text: I suspect the issue is that refundAgent has toolChoice set to 'required' alongside a system prompt forbidding unapproved refunds—when approval is declined, the agent is still forced to call a tool, so it loops back into calling approveRefund repeatedly instead of just replying. A declined refund should let the agent reply normally, so toolChoice likely needs to be 'auto' instead. I want to check the orders.json data for A-1001 too.

The refund agent sets `toolChoice: 'required'`, which would force a tool call on every turn, including after a decline. I'll check the orders data and how the middleware handles declined interrupts before deciding.

text:
Searching for toolChoice references in agent.js turns up nothing, so it seems the config is likely spread directly into the generate call rather than handled explicitly. I want to check how defineAgent passes its config through to confirm this.

Thinking about the actual bug scenario: when the supervisor declines approval, the model still has toolChoice set to 'required', so it's forced to call another tool rather than being able to respond with text explaining the decline — it'll keep calling approveRefund or other tools until it hits maxTurns. That matches the symptom of the agent looping or failing after a decline. The fix could be switching toolChoice to 'auto' so the model can reply with text after a decline, though I should also check whether updating the system prompt to explicitly handle the declined-approval case would be a cleaner fix than changing the tool-choice policy globally.
The turn loop doesn't reference `toolChoice` directly, so I need to confirm how the agent config reaches `generate`.

text:
I'm confirming that this is a prompt agent where toolChoice 'required' propagates through render to every generate call in the loop, forcing the model to emit a tool call on each turn within the multi-turn tool loop governed by maxTurns.

The likely fix is switching toolChoice to 'auto' so the model can reply with text after a decline instead of being forced to keep calling tools, which aligns with the expectation that a declined refund ends with a short customer-facing message.

I'll make the swap to 'auto', since that still preserves the approval guard since issueRefund stays gated behind the tool's own instructions. The loop symptoms all point consistently to this toolChoice setting being the root cause—forced tool-calling would explain repeated approval requests, order lookups, and eventual max-turns failures.

Before applying the fix, I should check the API key is set and run a typecheck with the local tsc binary to make sure nothing's broken, then proceed with the edit.

The refund agent is defined through `definePrompt`, so its `toolChoice: 'required'` applies to every model call in the agent loop, including the turn after a decline. I'll confirm the middleware doesn't override it, then make the fix.

text:
The middleware leaves toolChoice untouched and typecheck passes, with GEMINI_API_KEY available. I'm weighing whether a live API test is worthwhile given CLAUDE.md's restriction on running genkit commands directly, though a quick tsx verification script would be a reasonable check despite the token cost and potential non-determinism—the code evidence alone already feels fairly convincing.

I'll skip the live run since the code-level evidence is clear enough: the agent is defined with toolChoice 'required' at agents.ts:43, which applies to every generate call in the loop, forcing the model to keep emitting tool calls (approveRefund/lookupOrder/issueRefund) after a denial, looping until maxTurns: 6 — matching all three symptoms, while the triage agent correctly uses 'auto' at line 54. Now I'll write answer.json identifying src/agents.ts as the file and noting I verified this through code reading rather than execution.
The fix typechecks and the middleware doesn't override `toolChoice`. Now I'll write `answer.json`.

The root cause is `toolChoice: 'required'` on `refundAgent` in `src/agents.ts:43`. I changed it to `'auto'`.

Because the setting applies to every model call in the agent loop, the model must call a tool after a decline. Its only tools are `lookupOrder`, `approveRefund` and `issueRefund`, so it re-asks approval, re-looks-up the order, or hits `maxTurns: 6` and fails. That matches all three symptoms in the report. The triage agent already uses `'auto'`.

`npx tsc --noEmit` passes. I did not run the refund flow against Gemini, so the fix is confirmed by reading the code path, not by a live run. `answer.json` is written at the project root with the file, snippet, cause and evidence.
